# Rights and delivery

For asset rights, credits, subtitles and delivery checks.

## Core

- Deliver a `CREDITS` file naming every third-party asset (samples, music, fonts, images, the voice engine) with its source and licence; credit on screen where a licence requires it; tell the user `CREDITS` lists the licences and the material is their responsibility.
- When anything is spoken, offer an `.srt` in one line.
- `voyager media review FILE` measures loudness but flags only a true peak above 0 dBTP (clipping): check `audio.integratedLUFS` near −14 and `audio.truePeakDBTP` at or below −1 yourself. It also checks black frames and duration. Re-level with two-pass `loudnorm` (`TP=-1`, `linear=true`, the first pass's measured values) and review again before presenting. When the audio is a person's recording, review the processed voice stem (not the final mix with music) and pass the recording as `--audio-source`: review then flags a noise floor raised more than 15 dB or crushed dynamics; never force a very quiet recording to the target.
- To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use a video-understanding model with `voyager models run`; load `choose-media-model/references/understanding.md` for the paid upload route.

# Polished product films

Show the result and enough of the real interaction to explain its value.

Choose source material per scene: actual UI screenshots, short recordings of
meaningful motion, existing assets, or composed animation. Browser automation and
native integrations can prepare repeatable states without continuous recording.
A browser screenshot is downscaled to at most 1280 px wide by default; save a
frame for the film by resizing the tab `freeform` to the output size with `preview_resize`,
then `preview_snapshot` `save=true` with `screenshotSize: "full"`.
A `preview_recording` take is only as large as the docked preview panel: inset or
picture-in-picture, never full-bleed or pushed in.
Use verified outcomes when product responses vary.

For a physical product rendered in 3D, read
[product hero](product-hero.md) for its Blender pitfalls. To put a real recording
on a laptop, phone or monitor in a generated scene, read
[screen inserts](screen-inserts.md).

Make each text beat one claim, then the picture that proves it (a cold drink shows
condensation; a fast export shows the progress bar finishing).
Say the product name at the open and the close rather than repeating it as a message.
A product film is pictures first.

## Recorded scenes

Screen recording is macOS only; elsewhere use the user's own recordings.
For cross-app action, choose a
display or region that keeps the viewer oriented. For a self-demo, drive the actual Voyager interface with computer control
and record its real previews and behavior.

Capture complete action → response → result sequences, including playback. Native
operations must have a visible consequence in the captured UI. Separate debugging
from usable takes, and show a revision with one short matched comparison. Idle
windows, plan documents and job metadata do not substitute for product behavior.
Readable pauses on real UI are useful; recorded footage does not need the constant
motion of composed motion graphics. For recording and control mechanics, read
[recorded demos](../../use-computer/references/recorded-demos.md).

# Premium product hero films

Read when a physical product (a bottle, can, jar, device, watch) is the hero of a
3D launch or commercial film. For the story, claims and titles of any launch film, read
[product films](product-films.md). Engine, samples and render budget stay as
[edit-in-blender](../../edit-in-blender/SKILL.md) sets them.

## Pitfalls

- **Clear liquids need a bright zone behind them.** Keep a small, bright spot low
  behind the body (or bring the backdrop closer) in every dark shot.
- **EEVEE's screen-space refraction puts black bands through clear bottles.** Use
  Cycles for preview and final whenever clear glass or liquid is on screen.
- **Glossy floors mirror the softboxes.** Light-link the studio lights to the product
  (Blender 4.0+), or turn off their glossy ray visibility.
- **CJK text from Noto variable fonts renders blank in Blender.** Use static font
  files, or better, set the type in the edit.
- **A bump map derived from a product photo embosses JPEG noise.** Use a clean
  authored or procedural normal map, or none.
- **Web product photos are small (often about 400 px).** Upscale the label texture
  first ([make-image](../../make-image/SKILL.md)) and avoid label macros past 0.95 fill.

# Real screens in generated scenes

Put a real recording on a laptop, phone or monitor inside a generated scene.
A tutorial or inspiration may say "keep the camera locked"; that only made its
tracking easier. Do not copy it.

## Scene: moving and photographed

Start from a still and follow
[review stills before animating](../../make-ai-video/SKILL.md#review-stills-before-animating).
Get the photoreal look right in the still, then animate it with image-to-video.

Write the still prompt as a photograph:

- Name a real camera, lens and aperture ("full-frame camera, 50mm at f/2"), one
  motivated light source, and the time of day.
- Ask for lived-in detail: dust, fingerprints, worn keycaps, cable clutter, a
  slightly messy desk, uneven light falloff, natural shadows and film grain.
- Leave out "cinematic product film", "render", "3D", "studio" and "perfect".
  These words make the frame look like CG.
- Set the exposure so the screen does not clip. In a dark room it is the
  brightest thing in the frame. In daylight it is dimmer than the window.
- Ask for an evenly lit empty display with no text, no logos and no interface. Make
  it the recording's average colour: light grey for a light UI, dark slate for a
  dark UI. Keep a faint, natural reflection on the glass. The light it casts on
  the keyboard, hands and face should then match what you insert.
- All four inner screen corners stay visible. No hands or objects cross the screen.
  Ask for a uniform bezel with no camera notch. Image models often draw a MacBook
  notch anyway. If one appears, track the screen from its four outer corners,
  ignoring the notch, and composite the notch back over the insert as foreground.

For the animation prompt, give the shot one continuous camera move that the
viewer clearly notices, plus some ambient life. Video models under-deliver on
motion, so ask for more than you want and name where the move starts and ends:

- The move: a dolly push-in from a wide desk shot to the screen filling most of
  the frame; a lateral track with foreground objects sliding past in parallax;
  a 20–35° arc around the laptop; or a crane down from above the desk to eye
  level. Combine two when it suits the shot (arc while pushing in). Ease in and
  out, and finish the move on the screen while the key UI moment plays.
- Limits: all four corners stay in frame the whole time, and at its smallest the
  screen is still about 35% of the frame width. Avoid whip pans, handheld shake
  and focus pulls across the screen.
- Ambient life, chosen to fit the scene: steam, moving bokeh, headlights sweeping
  across the wall, cloud shadows, blinds shadows, rain on the window, a person
  passing out of focus, a plant moving in a breeze.

Check the plate before compositing. Across the shot, the tracked screen should
change width by at least 25% or its centre should travel at least 15% of the
frame width. Below that, the shot reads as static: tell the user and regenerate
with a stronger move. A static plate is fine only when the user asks for one.

## Track

When the screen is flat and evenly lit, find it in every frame: threshold it, take
the largest four-sided contour, and fit one line to each edge. When the camera
moves, don't fall back to the previous frame's corners on a miss. Re-seed from a
homography of bezel features (optical flow or ECC) instead. Smooth lightly
(sigma ≤ 1.5 frames). Draw the track over a contact sheet of the start, middle, end and worst
frame. In every frame, the corners stay within about 1 px of the inner bezel edge
at 1080p.

## Composite: photographed, not pasted

Treat the recording as light coming from a panel that this camera photographed.
Do these in order, all in linear light:

1. **Display response.** Never let the panel reach pure black or pure white. Lift
   the blacks slightly. Put UI white at about the empty panel's mean brightness,
   not above it. Pull the
   white point halfway toward the plate's screen tint.
2. **Panel falloff and lighting.** Blur the plate's empty-screen luminance, divide
   it by its mean, and multiply the insert by the result.
3. **Glass.** Median-filter and blur the plate first (about 12 px at 1080p),
   then keep only the broad reflections and glare (blurred minus heavily blurred).
   Screen-blend them over the insert at a low level (about 0.4). They should be
   a faint sheen on dark UI and almost gone on white.
4. **Optics.** Warp with an area filter from a supersampled source. Blur the insert until its edges are as soft as the bezel edge next to
   it (about 0.5 px at 1080p for an in-focus screen; more washes out small text). Add depth of field if the plate's focus changes, and motion blur from each
   frame's corner velocity. The insert must never be the sharpest thing in the
   frame.
5. **Grain.** Measure the noise in a flat area of the plate and add matching
   per-frame luma grain to the insert. Encode the whole frame in one pass.
6. **Edge and bloom.** Use a 1 px soft matte on the inner bezel edge. In a dark
   scene, let a bright UI bleed a faint halation onto the bezel.
7. **Spill.** Compare the insert's mean luminance in each frame with the plate's
   screen. Brighten or darken a soft spill mask in front of the screen (keyboard,
   desk, hands, face) by that ratio, within about ±20%. A cut from a white page to
   a dark terminal should visibly dim the keyboard.

Save the track, the compositor and the finishing settings with the project, so a
revised recording reuses them. A new camera move needs a new track.

## Review

Look at full-size stills from the start, middle and end of the move. Put a crop of
the screen next to a crop of the plate around it. Grain, softness, black level and
reflections should match. Then run the readability check in
[the skill](../SKILL.md#keep-the-interface-readable). If the key text won't read
at plate softness, push in closer or hold longer. Don't sharpen the insert past
the plate.

# Quick walkthroughs and tutorials

Browser automation can obtain clean
states, element bounds, screenshots, or short recordings; use the supported browser
tools rather than starting another automation stack. A preview recording is panel-sized;
for full-frame shots resize the tab to the output size, then `preview_snapshot`
`screenshotSize: "full"`; or, on Windows and
Linux, where Voyager can't record the screen, the user's own recordings. Native integrations can set
up desktop apps; use visible pointer control only when it helps the demonstration.

A quick founder update may work best as a real take with live narration and light
trimming. No launch-film storyboard,
rehearsal scene or multi-agent production pipeline is required.

When the user wants an interactive walkthrough, use available web authoring tools
to create a maintainable sequence or branching experience. Do not turn an explicitly
requested video into an interactive site. Do not invent a hosted demo service.

Readiness checks are better than fixed sleeps. Observe outcomes before
retrying an action that may have created, submitted, or purchased something.

---
name: make-product-demo
description: "Software walkthroughs, tutorials, app promos, launch videos and interactive demos from real product UI, screenshots or recordings; recording optional."
applications:
  - id: browser
    role: primary
  - id: remotion
    role: alternative
  - id: hyperframes
    role: alternative
  - id: resolve
    role: alternative
  - id: ffmpeg
    role: fallback
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: optional
  craft: [rights-and-delivery]
---

## First: check screen recording

If `<voyager_environment>` says screen recording is unavailable (Windows or Linux),
this is not optional: start your first reply, before any storyboard, plan or other
question, with one sentence like:

"Voyager can't record your screen on <your OS>, so for real footage of your app please
send a screen recording or full-size screenshots — meanwhile I'll build from <what you
have>."

Name the user's OS. Then keep going with what you have; don't wait for an answer.
Don't promise footage of their screen or app that Voyager can't film.

Use real behavior
and assets where applicable, combining browser automation, native integrations,
screenshots, recordings and composed animation. Record only when useful.

Choose a usable route: supported browser tooling for web interaction and screenshots, native
integrations for app operations, computer control for remaining UI work.

Screen recording is macOS only; computer control also works on Windows (not Linux). For browser frames, first `preview_resize` the tab `freeform` to the
output size, then `preview_snapshot` `save=true` with `screenshotSize: "full"`.

- [Quick walkthroughs and tutorials](references/walkthroughs.md): light production,
  live or separate narration, and interactive alternatives when appropriate.
- Generated narration: [voiceover](../voiceover/SKILL.md). Check `voyager voice agent capabilities`
  `narration` before scripting it; when narration is unavailable, make a captions-led cut.
- [Polished product films](references/product-films.md): authentic product states,
  clear transformation, composed motion, and targeted revisions.
- [Screen inserts](references/screen-inserts.md): a real recording on a device in a
  generated scene, with a moving camera and a photographed-looking composite.
- If recording: [recorded demos](../use-computer/references/recorded-demos.md) and
  [screen-capture](../screen-capture/SKILL.md).
- If their own footage has someone talking, [edit by text](../edit-video/SKILL.md) is available.
- For assembly, choose available [editing routes](../screen-capture/references/editing-routes.md),
  or [motion graphics](../make-motion-graphics/SKILL.md).
- Export review: [review](../make-ai-video/references/review.md).

## Keep the interface readable

Screens come from the product: the user's screenshots and recordings, a
capture you make, or the interface rebuilt in code from them
([product UI](../make-motion-graphics/references/product-ui.md)). Move them with
deterministic motion (pans, zooms, crops, masks, highlights, cursor paths) and set every headline, label and callout as real type. Never pass a
screenshot to an image-to-video, reference-to-video or text-to-video model, or ask
a model to draw the interface: its text comes back garbled. Generated clips are for
shots without product UI (an incidental screen stays off or unreadable). If the
user explicitly asks a model to animate or draw their interface, say once that its
text will not be exact, then generate those shots; the check below then covers only
the real screens. Without screenshots or access, ask for them before building.
Write English copy in US spelling unless the user, their brand kit or the project uses another variety.

Before delivering, unless the user said not to review, sample the export at
each moment UI text is on screen and compare against the source screens: labels
must read and match. Fix scale, crop, motion
blur or compression (a higher bitrate, a slower move, a tighter crop) and
re-export; after two fixes, tell the user which screen won't read at this size
and offer a tighter crop or a split.

A native timeline, code project, or reproducible assembly recipe can be the right
editable handoff.

## Let the product fill the frame

Before planning the scenes of a launch film or promo, read
[promotional treatment](../make-motion-graphics/references/promotional-treatment.md)
and [design like a motion designer](../make-motion-graphics/SKILL.md#design-like-a-motion-designer)
(no slideshow layouts, new kinetic type each scene, motifs that carry through).

The real screens are the picture. Run each recording or screenshot full-bleed or
nearly so, and move the camera into the part that matters: push in on the control
in use, pan along the flow, crop to the active region. A browser or device frame is
an occasional accent, never the container every scene sits in. A source shown
full-bleed or pushed in must be at least the output size. A `preview_recording` take
is the docked panel's on-screen size, so use it only as an inset or picture-in-picture,
never full-bleed. Change the layout
from scene to scene rather than repeating one template. Mascots, characters and
illustrations come only from the user's brand assets; never invent one. Keep
on-screen text to a short line that stays clear of the UI it describes.

Full-bleed goes only as far as the source's pixels: shown more than 1.5x its own
size, push-in included, a screen looks soft. A 1280x720 panel recording is the
limit for a still 1920x1080 frame. Record or capture at the delivery size or
larger; show a small screen smaller, or render a smaller frame. `media assemble`
warns about it; for a Remotion cut, review the render with the screens it shows
([edit-in-remotion](../edit-in-remotion/SKILL.md#review-the-render)).

## Look before building the cut

For a composed product film, before rendering the full cut, render stills from two
or three different scenes and a 2–4 s range of a camera move
([Remotion](../edit-in-remotion/SKILL.md#check-stills-and-a-short-range); in
another tool, export the same frames). Open them yourself and check each against
this bar:

- the real UI fills or nearly fills the frame, is the hero of the shot, and its
  text reads at delivery size;
- no two scenes share one layout: the screen crop and the caption or headline's
  position and treatment both change, not one caption template over new footage;
- no invented mascot or character, no pill or badge clutter, no screenshot
  floating in a browser window on a gradient;
- text is short and doesn't fight the UI;
- in the range render, the move eases onto the active region and settles there
  long enough to read its text, with no jump or stutter (stills can't show this,
  so the range is required).

Fix what fails and re-render those frames until all pass. Then present the first
passing still and the 2–4 s range with `voyager files present PATH --deliverable none --json`,
with a one-line progress note that does not embed it (chat shows each as a card), and build the cut without waiting for an
answer: this is your own check, not an approval. Present later renders you look at
as they finish, each under a new versioned name.

For continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use [watch and listen](../choose-media-model/references/understanding.md) (paid upload).
